description: A principal must approve a purchase and implementation plan for indoor-air-quality monitors in the science wing, including the number of monitors, installation scope, funding source, alert threshold, and health-review procedure, with input from facilities, the business office, and the school nurse.

shared_context.S1: The school is considering a vendor's indoor-air-quality monitoring system for the science wing.
shared_context.S2: The vendor offers a six-monitor package and a nine-monitor package.
shared_context.S3: The preliminary purchase discussion has focused on the cheaper six-monitor package, which costs $3,100; the nine-monitor package costs $4,320.
shared_context.S4: Dr. Lena Morris gives final approval for the purchase and its implementation plan.
shared_context.S5: The school's routine pre-purchase review includes a facilities check, a funding review, and a health review with the facilities manager, business office manager, and school nurse.

PF1.text: Mr. Bell's inspection found nine science-wing classrooms that each need a monitor because the rooms have separate ventilation zones; he completed the inspection this week, but the room-by-room report has not yet been entered into the purchasing worksheet.

PF2.text: Ms. Shah confirmed that a restricted capital account has exactly enough approved funding for the $4,320 nine-monitor package, and no general-fund transfer is needed; she verified the ledger this week, but the finance memo is awaiting the pre-purchase review.

PF3.text: Nurse Ruiz's review of the student health plans shows that the monitors' alerts must be set at 1,000 ppm carbon dioxide and reviewed by the nurse weekly during the first quarter; she completed that review this week, but has not yet added the health settings to the implementation plan.

acceptance_conditions: The nine-monitor package must be purchased.
One monitor must be installed in each of the nine science-wing classrooms.
The restricted capital account must be used as the funding source.
No general-fund transfer may be required.
The monitor alerts must be set at 1,000 ppm carbon dioxide.
A facilities installation commitment must be recorded.
A funding-coding commitment must be recorded.
A weekly nurse-review commitment for the first quarter must be recorded.
The nurse review schedule must be weekly during the first quarter.
The health-plan fact must be cited in the justification after it is spoken aloud.

content_checks.C3: 'nine' in decisions['installation_scope'] and 'classroom' in decisions['installation_scope'] and 'science wing' in decisions['installation_scope']
content_checks.C5: decisions['funding_source'] in ['restricted capital account', 'Restricted capital account']
content_checks.C7: any(c['target'] == 'Mr. Aaron Bell' and 'nine' in c['detail'] and 'classroom' in c['detail'] for c in commitments) or ('nine' in decisions['installation_scope'] and 'classroom' in decisions['installation_scope'] and 'science wing' in decisions['installation_scope'])
content_checks.C9: decisions['funding_source'] in ['restricted capital account', 'Restricted capital account'] and decisions['general_fund_transfer'] == False
content_checks.C10: 'weekly' in decisions['nurse_review_schedule'] and 'first quarter' in decisions['nurse_review_schedule']
content_checks.C11: 'weekly' in decisions['nurse_review_schedule'] and 'first quarter' in decisions['nurse_review_schedule']

decisive_facts.why: The facilities inspection changes the required system from six monitors to exactly nine and changes the installation scope to all nine science-wing classrooms.

The ledger review changes the approved purchase total to exactly $4,320, changes the funding source to the restricted capital account, changes the transfer decision to no general-fund transfer, and requires coding the purchase to that account.
The health-plan review changes the alert threshold to exactly 1,000 ppm, adds weekly nurse review during the first quarter, and changes the required review schedule to weekly during that period.
